blind_spots.blind_spot: The capture device is a commercial phone, on installations where commercial phones with cameras are the problem
blind_spots.operator_reality: Photographing electronic parts inside an Air Force depot bay or supply warehouse means a camera-enabled device in a controlled area, and the resulting images of part markings, lot codes, and vendor stamps are CUI and often export-controlled. In practice the app has to live on a government-issued, MDM-enrolled device with an ATO and an IL-appropriate backend — a 12-to-18-month path that has nothing to do with building the model.
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: In the commercial energy-audit business the auditor's own iPhone IS the device and the photos are nobody's controlled data; the entire product was born from that assumption ('Photos were on Herb's phone').
blind_spots.evidence_quote: EMPEQ is proposing a solution that uses machine learning to identify electronic parts through a secure handheld device such as an iPhone, iPad, tablet, or Android.

blind_spots.blind_spot: Enrichment and 'single source of truth' assume a live round trip to their cloud
blind_spots.operator_reality: The places counterfeit parts actually get inspected — a hangar bay, a warehouse deep in a hardened structure, a shipboard storeroom, a forward supply point — are RF holes with no usable connectivity. If identification requires the phone to reach the enrichment backend, the technician gets a spinner instead of a verdict, and the whole workflow reverts to the legal pad the founders were trying to kill. On-device inference with deferred, conflict-safe sync is a different architecture than the pipeline they built.
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: Commercial buildings have WiFi and LTE; nothing in 200 rooftop audits ever forced them to design for a denied or disconnected capture session.
blind_spots.evidence_quote: Turn fragmented infrastructure data into real-time, reliable insights. EMPEQ meets your data where it is—and transforms it into action.

blind_spots.blind_spot: A counterfeit call is a quality record, not an insight
blind_spots.operator_reality: When the app says a part is counterfeit, that output enters a supply-chain quality process — the lot gets quarantined, a GIDEP alert may follow, a vendor gets challenged, and someone signs their name to the determination. That demands a stated false-positive/false-negative rate, model-version traceability on every call, an audit trail that survives a discrepancy investigation, and a named government authority who owns the disposition. Their language treats output as decision support ('insights', 'confidence'), which is exactly the framing that stalls at the transition review.
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: For an energy model, a wrong SEER rating costs a re-visit; the product's whole design point is speed over evidentiary rigor, and no commercial customer ever asked them to defend a call.
blind_spots.evidence_quote: EMPEQ powers the shift from manual guesswork to verified, structured insights—ready for automation, compliance, and strategic planning.

opener_hook: Your Phase II proposes counterfeit-part identification on 'an iPhone, iPad, tablet, or Android' — and the only two roles open on empeq.co right now are Senior Strategic Account Executives.
what_they_do: SaaS that turns photos and messy spreadsheets of physical equipment into structured, enriched asset records; adapting the same capture tech to Air Force counterfeit-part detection.
